title: Renewal Surge Response — Rapid Triage & Exec Escalation Template
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, ready-to-run template for rapid response when a renewal shows sudden deterioration ("surge" in risk). Use for the first 72 hours of triage and the subsequent 30-day save window. The doc is intentionally prescriptive — sequence of steps + fillable templates for exec brief and customer outreach.

Scope / When to use:
- Use when any of the following happen within a 30-day window before renewal:
  - Net product usage drops >40% week-over-week for key seats or orgs.
  - Spike in Severity 1/2 support tickets tied to regressions or latency that affect production features (>=3 distinct incidents in 7 days).
  - Customer signals (email/CSM note) requesting contract downgrades or exploring alternatives.
  - Billing disputes or a loaded procurement/legal pause.

Quick definition — "Surge": a compact cluster of signals that moves an account from Green/Yellow to Red in under 7 days. This template is optimized for those fast-moving cases.

Signal Matrix (quick checklist):
- Product signals:
  - Usage: MAU, active seats, tokens/day by route (include Hosted/Dedicated/Private split).
  - Latency/P99 increases vs baseline >2x for critical endpoints.
  - Errors: generation truncation, model fallback frequency, streaming disconnects.
- Support signals:
  - Number of Sev1/2 tickets in window, time to first response, time to resolution.
- Commercial signals:
  - Renewal paused/decision-maker unavailable, PO delays, downgrade messages.
- Sentiment signals:
  - CSM notes: tone negative, explicit statements of "considering alternatives".

Risk Scoring (0-10 quick rubric):
- 0-3 Low: stable usage, minor tickets, renewal on track.
- 4-6 Medium: usage down 10-40%, 1-2 high-severity incidents, procurement questions.
- 7-10 High: usage drop >40% or >=3 high-sev incidents, exec-level complaints, legal/procurement escalation.

Triage — First 48 hours (owners + checklist):
1) Intake (CSM) — immediate: record signals in account tracker (owner: CSM) — required fields: risk score, top-3 causes suspected, top internal contacts.
2) Fast tech audit (SRE/SE) — 12h: ingest logs for last 7 days, verify latency regressions, model variant fallbacks, capacity constraints (dedicated pool saturation).
3) Quick commercial check (AM/RevOps) — 12h: confirm contract dates, PO status, billing disputes.
4) Customer outreach (CSM) — 24h: low-friction check-in (scripted) to acknowledge, ask for permission for deeper triage, set expectation for next touch.
5) Escalation call (if risk >=7) — 48h: cross-functional sync w/ SRE, SE, Product PM, AM, and head of CS.

Rapid Mitigation Playbook (by effort & impact):
- Tier A (Immediate, low friction; 0–48h):
  - Issue: transient latency or routing glitch. Play: reroute traffic to healthy region or promote compatible model variant for affected endpoints. Owner: SRE.
  - Issue: missing caching affecting request volume. Play: enable prefix/KV caching for top routes, apply temporary TTL. Owner: Runtime Eng + SE.
  - Customer comms: proactive note + ETA for next update.
- Tier B (Medium effort; 2–7 days):
  - Issue: model quality regression after rollout. Play: rollback to previous pinned model version, open runbook to repro/regress. Owner: Product + SE.
  - Issue: Dedicated pool throughput limits. Play: temporarily bump reserved capacity (burst) or move high-priority routes to burst pool. Owner: Infra + Sales ops.
  - Compensation option: limited SLA credit or temporary discounted overage to preserve relationship (coordinated with RevOps).
- Tier C (Exec-level; 7–30 days):
  - Issue: systemic reliability or contract-scale mismatch. Play: offer on-site/virtual deep-obs engagement (dedicated engineering rotation), contractual concession (short-term discount, extended pilot), or executive sponsor intro. Owner: Head of CS + Customer Exec Sponsor.

Save Plays (concrete templates):
- "One-week stability pledge": commit 7-day dedicated SRE window + daily sync + root cause update. Includes 2-hour on-call slot for immediate ops.
- "Quality rollback + guardrails": revert model change, add canary gates for 10% traffic, hold subsequent rollouts for 30 days.
- "Adopt Optimize trial": grant 3 months of Redwood Optimize tailored suggestions and apply quantization recommendations to cut unit costs (value prop: save + performance).
- "Executive alignment package": 2 executive council meetings (Redwood SVP + customer VP), revised SLA, and joint postmortem within 30 days.

Escalation Ladder (names & roles — fill per account):
- CSM (first responder) — name, email, phone.
- Technical lead (SE/SRE) — name, escalation contact.
- AM / RevOps (commercial) — name.
- Head of CS — Priya Malhotra (escalation contact).
- VP Sales / Customer Exec Sponsor — internal name placeholder.

Exec Brief (one-pager template — copy into email/slide):
- Subject: RED ALERT — Renewal risk for [AccountName] (Renewal: yyyy-mm-dd)
- TL;DR: risk score X/10 — immediate next steps (triage complete? mitigation chosen?)
- Customer impact: users affected, lost ARR risk estimate, product/functionality impacted.
- Root cause hypothesis: short bullets (e.g., model rollback caused quality drop; Dedicated capacity saturation).
- Actions taken: list with owners + ETA.
- Proposed escalate actions: exec sponsor, credit, engineering rotation, contractual concession.
- Ask of exec: decision required (yes/no) on proposed concession and assignment of sponsor.

Internal Communication Snippets (copy-paste):
- Slack to #cs-escalations: "RED: [Acct] risk 8/10. CSM Priya, SE Lucas, SRE Maya engaged. First tech audit shows P99 latency 2.8x baseline and model fallback rate 19%. Need exec decision on 30% temporary credit and dedicated engineering rotation. Call in 40m."
- Initial customer email: "Hi [Name], we heard your concerns — we’re triaging now. I’ll share our findings within 24h and propose immediate mitigations. Can we schedule a 30m call today? — [CSM]"

QBR Snapshot (to drop into QBR slide):
- Renewal status: At risk / Monitor / On track
- Risk score: X/10
- Primary driver: (Product / Commercial / Support)
- Actions underway: list w/owner + due date
- ARR at risk (USD) + probability-adjusted expected loss

Action Tracker (minimum fields — put into tracker sheet):
- Action ID, short description, owner, due date, status, mitigation tier, notes

Post-save retro & decisioning:
- Required within 7 days of stabilization: root cause write-up, timeline of events, customer-signed closure statement (if concession given).
- If a concession was granted >$50k ARR impact: prepare exec review with lessons learned and prevention plan.

Templates & Notes to CSMs (practical tips):
- Always capture logs/metrics snapshot before making config changes — snapshot timestamped and attached to the ticket.
- If offering a commercial concession, copy RevOps on the first note.
- Use the "One-week stability pledge" only once per customer per 12-month period without VP approval.

Open questions / TODOs (draft stage):
- Decide standard maximum concession tiers by renewal size (TBD with RevOps).
- Finalize who can sign off on dedicated engineering rotations (head of infra vs. head of cs).
- Add canned observability dashboard link for common failure patterns.

Appendix: quick checklists for handoff to Renewals team:
- Attach final risk score card and all audit artifacts.
- Indicate whether customer accepted offered mitigate, demanded termination, or asked to pause renewal.
- Flag for legal if contract deviation >2 months or concession >25% of ARR.

Notes (working):
- Draft language intentionally concise for exec consumption — keep <6 bullets in TL;DR.
- This doc is a living template — copy into account folder and update 'Escalation Ladder' with names for each account preemptively (pre-wiring is high ROI).

Example quick timeline for a high-risk case (hours/days):
- Hour 0: Signal hits (CSM flags), intake added.
- Hour 6: Fast tech audit started.
- Hour 12: Customer outreach + confirm renewal window.
- Hour 24: Initial mitigation (Tier A) applied if applicable.
- Hour 48: Cross-functional escalation call if risk >=7.
- Day 3–7: Tier B interventions.
- Week 2–4: Tier C (exec engagement / contractual).

Owner notes: Priya — will pilot this with 3 high-touch enterprise accounts in Q1; feedback loop to update concession thresholds and final approval matrix.

End of template.
